criteria.name: Thesis and position
criteria.description: a clear, arguable position on the question that stays consistent through the essay.

criteria.name: Evidence and reasoning
criteria.description: specific, relevant support (facts, examples, logic) that actually backs the claims, including a fair answer to the other side.

criteria.name: Organization
criteria.description: a logical order with an introduction, paragraphs that each do a job, transitions, and a conclusion.

criteria.name: Language and style
criteria.description: precise word choice, varied sentences, and a tone suited to persuading a reader.

criteria.name: Interpretation
criteria.description: a defensible claim about how the theme is developed, going beyond plot summary.

criteria.name: Textual evidence
criteria.description: accurate, specific references to events, characters or lines from the play.

criteria.name: Analysis
criteria.description: explains how the evidence supports the claim, rather than only saying what happens.

criteria.name: Organization and style
criteria.description: logical structure, transitions and clear academic prose, including correct mechanics.

criteria.name: Narrative development
criteria.description: a clear sequence of events with concrete detail and sensible pacing.

criteria.name: Reflection and insight
criteria.description: genuine thought about what the experience taught the writer and why it mattered.

criteria.name: Voice and word choice
criteria.description: a natural, distinctive voice and vivid, precise language.
